item.title: Takeaways from UH's win at West Virginia: Cougars bounce back, Keisean Henderson arrives
item.description: Houston Cougars wide receiver Amare Thomas (0) runs to the endzone for a touchdown after a catch against West Virginia Mountaineers during the first half of an NCAA college football game, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Morgantown, W.Va. (AP Photo/William Wotring) (William Wotring/Associated Press) MORGANTOWN, W.Va. - Five takeaways from No. 20 Houston's 34-31 victory over West Virginia on Saturday: Bounce-back win How would the Cougars respond after a disappointing performance in a 42-32 loss at Colorado ? The Cougars showed plenty of fight and, while the defense still showed some cracks and the offense sputtered at times, it was a Big 12 road win. UH also remains in position to reach the 10-win mark in consecutive seasons for the first time in program history. "We had to flush it out and come back stronger," running back Makhi Hughes said. "That's what we did." Look to the future All the talk has been about the Keisean Henderson era beginning in 2027. Well, that's still the case, but UH fans got a sneak peek when the true freshman made his first career start in place of injured fifth-year senior Conner Weigman . Henderson had some impressive moments (his 68-yard touchdown pass to Amare Thomas on the third play of the game) but it was what he didn't do that should be praised. The heralded freshman knew when to throw the ball away. He knew when not to try and do too much. He trusted his pass protection and had enough patience to stay in the pocket long enough to see things develop. He also showed his ability to run, including an 18-yard keeper. His game management down the stretch resembled that of a veteran, not a first-year quarterback who had been limited to 17 snaps all season. The future is bright for Henderson. Henderson averaged 3.19 seconds to throw on all dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Only one of Henderson's two sacks was credited to the offensive line. "We got a couple of blitzes and got a little pressure on him, but outside of that, it was way too much time to throw the ball," West Virginia coach Rich Rodriguez said. We'll give the line a pass for the three false starts. Run, run, run That seems to be what the UH defense has seen in the past month. It was another heavy dose of runs Saturday as the Cougars allowed a season-high 329 yards to the Mountaineers. That followed the 249 yards allowed by UH in a double-digit loss at Colorado. The Boston Red Sox continue making changes to their roster, and their latest trade involves a pitcher who barely had an opportunity to contribute during the 2026 season. Boston traded right-hander Johan Oviedo to the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday in exchange for minor league left-hander Luke Dotson and a player to be named later or cash considerations. The move was part of a busy stretch for chief baseball officer Craig Breslow, who has already made several transactions as the organization prepares for the 2027 season. Oviedo's departure is particularly interesting because of the circumstances surrounding his brief time in Boston. The 28-year-old appeared in just one major league game for the Red Sox this season before an elbow injury essentially ended his year. Now, rather than bringing him back for another opportunity, Boston has decided to move in a different direction. Oviedo's Red Sox Tenure Never Got Started Oviedo arrived in Boston after previously pitching for the St. Louis Cardinals and Pittsburgh Pirates. He made 32 starts for Pittsburgh in 2023, posting a 4.31 ERA and demonstrating that he could handle a regular role in a major league rotation. The Red Sox have dealt Johan Oviedo to the Diamondbacks, per @ByRobertMurray. The right-hander pitched 3 2/3 innings in relief against Houston on March 30 before being placed on the injured list with a right elbow strain. He eventually made a rehabilitation appearance for Triple-A Worcester in September but never returned to the major league mound for the Red Sox. That left Boston with limited opportunities to evaluate how Oviedo might fit into its future pitching plans. Arizona now gets the opportunity to determine whether he can regain his previous form. item.title: Colts revealed to have turned down great trade offer from Ravens for Daniel Jones
item.description: Colts revealed to have turned down great trade offer from Ravens for Daniel Jones originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts managed to ship off a lot of players at the NFL trade deadline, but they notably didn't make a few other roster moves with Daniel Jones and Jonathan Taylor. Of the two, their star running back would've brought back the best return. But, since he's under contract beyond 2026, the Colts didn't have to move him. Jones, on the other hand, was released after Week 11, and clearly should've been traded. But, what could they have even got for Jones? According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Colts had a great trade offer on the table for Jones that they turned down in what's now very clearly a huge missed opportunity for the Colts. Colts trade offer they turned down from Ravens for Daniel Jones revealed "The Ravens offered the Colts a fourth-round draft pick for Daniel Jones and a fifth-round pick, with the condition that fifth-rounder would be returned to Indianapolis if Baltimore advanced to the playoffs," Schefter reports. "Minnesota also had interest in Jones. Indy held him, then released him." This is a brutal report from Schefter for the Colts. They had a chance to land a strong return for Jones that, at the very least, would've been a nice upgrade from the fifth to the fourth round. While that alone might not be worth trading a team's starting quarterback, in the Colts case, Jones only remained the starter for two games after that trade was declined by Indianapolis. MORE : Grading NFL trade deadline debuts, from Kirk Cousins' Vikings return to Josh Downs' impressive day There was a scenario where the Colts accept that trade, and the Ravens make the playoffs, and the Colts walk away with a fourth- and fifth-round pick for Jones, whom they would've released. Instead, the Colts didn't get anything for Jones, as they cut him one day after Thursday Night Football, and over one week after the NFL trade deadline had passed. It's about as clear of a missed trade opportunity as it can get. Combined with not trading Grover Stewart and Taylor despite solid offers being on the table, the Colts arguably made three big mistakes at this year's trade deadline. item.description: Celtics Suffer Stunning Collapse As Kings End Eight-Game Losing Streak originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics couldn't have asked for a much better opportunity to end their losing streak Saturday night. Sacramento entered the game with one victory in its first 15 games, had lost eight consecutive contests and hadn't won at home all season. Boston still found a way to lose. Keegan Murray scored on a putback with five seconds remaining, lifting the Kings to a stunning 97-96 victory at Golden 1 Center. The Celtics led 54-41 at halftime and appeared positioned to take care of business against one of the NBA's struggling teams. Instead, Boston endured a disastrous third quarter that completely changed the game. The defeat was Boston's third consecutive loss and arguably its most frustrating of the season. Third-Quarter Disaster Changes Everything The Celtics controlled much of the first half despite playing without Jayson Tatum, Derrick White and Mitchell Robinson. Final Score https://t.co/7yfWfbrfgZ — Boston Celtics (@celtics) November 22, 2026 Boston opened the game with a 10-0 run and maintained a comfortable advantage entering halftime. Then everything changed. Sacramento outscored Boston 35-13 in the third quarter, turning a 13-point deficit into a nine-point lead. The Celtics missed all 13 of their three-point attempts during the period, an extraordinary shooting collapse that allowed the Kings to seize momentum. Boston finished the game shooting just 22% from beyond the arc despite attempting 58 three-pointers. Those numbers help explain how a team that appeared comfortably in control suddenly found itself fighting to avoid an embarrassing defeat. The Celtics eventually recovered enough to give themselves a chance in the final seconds. They just couldn't finish. item.title: “Wemby Coming for Luka MVP Trophy”, “Statpadding in Garbage Mins”: NBA Fans Divided After Victor Wembanyama Drops 50 Points Against Zion-Less Pelicans
item.description: Victor Wembanyama © X/ @spurs Victor Wembanyama produced another monster performance as the San Antonio Spurs blew out the New Orleans Pelicans 114-91 on Saturday. Wembanyama posted 50 points, 19 rebounds, four steals, and five blocks. While some fans downplayed his numbers due to the stature of the Pelicans, who fell to 5-13, others were thrilled to see Wemby’s all-around brilliance. “Wemby coming for Luka MVP trophy,” one fan commented . “Statpadding in garbage mins,” another fan claimed . With Zion Williamson (thigh) and Trey Murphy III (knee) sidelined, the Spurs established control in the first half, taking a 61-45 lead into the break. In the second half, San Antonio continued to shoot at a high rate, doing enough to maintain its sizable advantage. The Spurs held the Pelicans to 36.7% shooting from the field and 22.9% from beyond the arc. Helping Wembanyama on the scoring end were Stephon Castle (19 points, six assists), Devin Vassell, and Keldon Johnson, who each put up 10 points. The win keeps the Spurs in step with the Lakers, with whom they share a Western Conference-leading 14-3 record. “I’m Not Very Good at Stat-Padding”: Victor Wembanyama Appears to Take a Shot at “Peers” After 50-Piece vs. Pelicans In Victor Wembanyama’s eyes, he wasn’t putting up numbers for the sake of putting up numbers. In his post-game interview, Wembanyama seemed to take a shot at other NBA players who might have been toying with their stats. “Unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat-padding.” While other NBA players might have something to say about that, it’s hard to argue when the 7-foot-4 star dominates games as thoroughly as he did in the Spurs-Pelicans outing. item.title: Former Real Madrid star urges Mourinho to hand more minutes to Carlos Espi: ‘He’s a problem solver’
item.description: Former Real Madrid star urges Mourinho to hand more minutes to Carlos Espi: ‘He’s a problem solver’ Speaking on COPE (h/t Defensa Central ), former Real Madrid goalkeeper Santi Canizares has urged Jose Mourinho to hand a greater role to young striker Carlos Espi. This comes after the summer arrival came up clutch for Los Blancos against Celta Vigo on Saturday, scoring the match-winning goal at the Santiago Bernabeu. Having come on as a substitute against the Galician outfit in the 79th minute, the 21-year-old Spaniard found the back of the net six minutes later to help Real Madrid secure a 2-1 win. Canizares wants a more prominent role for Espi Since joining Real Madrid from Levante last summer, Espi has had to settle for a secondary role, given that Kylian Mbappe has been the undisputed starter at centre-forward. In all, the towering striker has played only 62 minutes this season for the club, across 12 matches, but has chipped in with four goals already , which include three match-winners against Espanyol, Elche, and now Celta Vigo. Carlos Espi has excelled in his limited opportunities. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) And Canizares acknowledged that the youngster is unlikely to displace Mbappe from the starting line-up. However, he questioned why he could not receive more playing time in matches that are already under control. “He can’t be a starter because Mbappe is there, but there are many minutes in the second half where Madrid is winning 2-0 or 3-0 with half an hour left,” he said. “It would be fair for him to get more playing time, and there are ways to find it,” the former goalkeeper added. Canizares compares Espi to Joselu Canizares then went on to compare Espi with former Real Madrid striker Joselu, who also became known for his impact as a penalty-box striker from the bench. Real Madrid’s new super-sub. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) But the former shot-stopper believes that the 21-year-old is much better than the veteran forward, as he said: “For me, Carlos Espi is a much better striker than Joselu. Every goal he scores is worth points; he’s a problem solver, and it’s the worst thing that can happen to you if you’re winning against Madrid, when this player comes on.” Further highlighting the youngster’s attributes, he added: “Espi is a player who has everything, he can play in all systems and has the aura of Real Madrid, of epic moments.” Despite his admiration for Espi, Canizares was far less impressed with Real Madrid’s overall display against Celta. “Real Madrid weren’t a good team today; they only won thanks to the individual talent of their players,” he argued. “Real Madrid’s defensive system can’t handle the movement of the players in front of them,” he noted.

item.description: Elias Lindholm Delivers Historic Performance As Bruins Outlast Capitals originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Bruins needed Elias Lindholm to be good Saturday night. They probably weren't expecting him to deliver one of the most remarkable individual performances in franchise history. Lindholm scored four goals and added an assist as Boston defeated the Washington Capitals 7-5 at TD Garden. The veteran forward recorded his third career hat trick and first with the Bruins, finishing with a career-high five points. His four goals matched Boston's franchise record for goals in a single game. David Pastrnak added a goal and two assists, while Morgan Geekie and Charlie McAvoy each contributed three assists. Jeremy Swayman made 30 saves as the Bruins improved to 15-7-1 and earned their second consecutive victory. The performance was particularly meaningful for Lindholm, who has quietly become one of Boston's most important offensive contributors. Lindholm's Historic Night Creates Unusual Moment The Bruins trailed 1-0 when Lindholm scored his first goal on the power play midway through the opening period. He added another goal in the second period before completing his hat trick with a deflection that gave Boston a 5-4 advantage late in the frame. Hey Elias, how many you score tonight? https://t.co/XBXi1Y6XIV — Boston Bruins (@NHLBruins) November 22, 2026 What happened next was almost as memorable as the goal itself. Only one hat initially landed on the ice after Lindholm's third goal. Even Pastrnak later acknowledged that he hadn't immediately realized his teammate had completed a hat trick. The confusion didn't last long. Lindholm scored again early in the third period, redirecting another Pastrnak shot to extend Boston's lead to 6-4. This time, the crowd responded with considerably more enthusiasm. The fourth goal capped a remarkable night for a player whose contributions often extend beyond the scoresheet. item.title: Chelsea facing huge injury scare after Leeds United defeat
item.description: Chelsea facing huge injury scare after Leeds United defeat Moises Caicedo Injury Adds to Chelsea Problems After Leeds Defeat Chelsea have another problem to manage, and this one matters. Moises Caicedo went down early in the defeat to Leeds at Stamford Bridge, and Xabi Alonso admitted the club will need more time before understanding the full extent of the injury. The midfielder pulled up just after the 20-minute mark, with no obvious contact in the moment that ended his game. He received treatment and tried to continue, but was eventually replaced by Jordan Henderson. For a player who has already had fitness issues across the season, it is a worrying development. Caicedo setback hits Chelsea midfield Caicedo had only just returned after another physical concern on international duty. He asked to come off at half-time in Ecuador’s 2-0 win over Bolivia, yet was still cleared to start against Leeds. Early in the match he was involved in a series of heavy challenges and also needed treatment after landing awkwardly on his back. None of that helps the picture. Alonso was clear that Chelsea do not yet have answers. Instead, they have another wait, another assessment, and another key player in doubt at a point when the squad is already stretched. Photo IMAGO Xabi Alonso reacts to loss of momentum The timing mattered. Chelsea were still level when Caicedo went off, and for a while they looked in control. Emmanuel Emegha put them ahead, but Noah Okafor responded quickly. From there, Chelsea folded. Okafor added a second and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted from the spot to seal a painful result. After the match, Alonso said: “It went wrong after the equaliser, after the change (with) Moi, we completely lost the momentum. Until then, we were doing okay, I think that we were creating, playing a lot on the pitch, we were coming out of the pressure. “But from that moment, they started believing and we started not believing. “And after that, we never got the good feeling mentality in any moment and we were not able to come for the pressure and we didn’t get close to their goal, so it completely changed.” Reece James and Maxence Lacroix latest That matters even more because Chelsea are already without Joao Pedro, Maxence Lacroix and Reece James. Alonso suggested Lacroix is closer to returning than James, saying: “I think that Max has a better chance than Reece. It’s not definitely that Reece won’t be back before then, but Max has a better chance.” Right now, Chelsea need clarity on Caicedo. Until they get it, the concern is obvious.

item.title: MotoGP Portuguese GP: Marc Marquez crowned 2026 champion as Marco Bezzecchi wins tense race
item.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez sealed the 2026 MotoGP title with a conservative ride to eighth at the Portuguese Grand Prix, as Marco Bezzecchi led a 1-2-3 finish for Aprilia. Having missed out on a chance to seal the title in both the Qatar Grand Prix and the Portimao sprint, Marquez only needed to finish inside the top nine on Sunday to secure the championship. While the Ducati rider led the race on the opening lap with a rapid getaway, he quickly dropped down the order, taking a safe approach following his surprise crash in Saturday’s contest. Although Bezzecchi recovered from a poor start to complete a double win at Portimao, with Jorge Martin finishing right behind second, it wasn’t enough to deny Marquez a title that had seemed inevitable since Martin’s crash at Phillip Island last month. Crossing the finish line in eighth, the Spaniard claimed his eighth MotoGP title, surpassing former rival Valentino Rossi and drawing level with Giacomo Agostini as the most successful rider in premier class history. Including his titles in the 125cc and 250cc categories, Marquez now has 10 world championships to his name, putting him third on the all-time list behind Agostini (15) and Angel Nieto (13). At the start of the race, Marquez made a brilliant launch from second on the grid, muscling past polesitter Bezzecchi to grab the lead. Bezzecchi, meanwhile, continued to tumble down the order on the opening lap, dropping as low as fifth as Raul Fernandez grabbed second. Meanwhile, Martin was on the move from seventh on the grid, jumping to fourth at the start before passing a recovering Bezzecchi under braking at the start of lap 2. This left three Aprilias chasing race leader Marquez, who had initially opened up a gap on the opening lap as his rivals fought among themselves. But the Ducati rider suddenly lost pace as the second lap began, with Fernandez, Martin and Bezzecchi all passing him in quick succession to establish an Aprilia 1-2-3. Among the three, Fernandez initially appeared as the quickest Aprilia, before Bezzecchi surged to the front, passing both Martin and Fernandez to take the lead on lap 15. Meanwhile, Marquez continued to drop down the order, losing further places to di Giannantonio, Ai Ogura and Brad Binder over the next 15 laps. This left him in ninth place - the minimum place he needed to secure to put the championship out of his rivals’ hands. As long as Martin was not winning the race, even a 14th place would have sufficed in their title battle. While Aprilia appeared to discuss manufacturer orders to orchestrate the result and keep Martin in the title fight, Bezzecchi was ultimately never asked to order position, having built a comfortable lead of three seconds. Bezzecchi went on to win the race with a comfortable margin to make it three victories in four races, with Martin taking the chequered flag in second after fending off a late attack from Fernandez. item.description: A European MMA show ended in catastrophe when its main event was cancelled at the 11th hour due to a backstage injury to the defending champion. Mateusz Legierski was due to defend his lightweight title against veteran fighter Ivan Buchinger at Oktagon 98 but tore his hamstring in the warm-up, forcing the headline bout to be scrapped. “Unfortunately, the Oktagon 98 main event will not take place,” a statement read. “Mateusz Legierski suffered an injury during his warm-up and was rushed to the hospital. He tore his hamstring and was forced to pull out of the bout.” Unfortunately, the OKTAGON 98 main event will not take place. Mateusz Legierski suffered an injury during his warm-up and was rushed to the hospital. He tore his hamstring and was forced to pull out of the bout. pic.twitter.com/z5CdEEgtRm — OKTAGON (@OktagonOfficial) November 21, 2026 Legierski was filmed being tended to by medics in his dressing room, where he was put onto a stretcher before being taken out of the Werk Arena in Trinec, Czech Republic. Buchinger, who was preparing for his 57th professional fight, was then called out to the cage in his fight attire to give his reaction. "This never happened to me,” Buchinger said. “Very disappointed, I was very well prepared, but unfortunately we have to come to terms with this situation. “I wish him a speedy recovery and hope this match will take place after that.” Asked whether he would accept another bout quickly or wait for another title fight, Buchinger said: “I am ready. I have been training hard for this match to get the belt. “I think I was very well prepared even though the [weight] classes were what they were. I came to get that belt.” The cancellation meant 24-year-old prospect Jakub Batfalsky’s split-decision win over Ayton De Paepe ended up closing the curtain on the event. Oktagon holds the record for the most-attended MMA event outside of Japan in history and attracted 58,000 fans to its marquee show of the year at Eintracht Frankfurt’s Deutsche Bank Park in September.

item.title: Lillard’s Warning Almost Kept Giannis Out Of Miami Heat
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images According to Yahoo Sports , Giannis Antetokounmpo nearly remained in Milwaukee. A new report reveals that Damian Lillard provided the Greek superstar with guidance that almost scuttled the deal. Lillard recognized how rapidly fan adoration can disappear once an athlete leaves their original franchise. This honest discussion nearly prompted Giannis to rethink the trade to Miami. Leaning on his own suffering, Lillard warned Giannis against leaving a long-term home. He joined the Bucks in 2023 but suffered an Achilles injury that ended his time there. This unsuccessful stint sent Lillard back to the Trail Blazers this past summer. He told Antetokounmpo that “They’re not going to always love on you like the way they will at home.” The warning resonated deeply given Giannis’s 13-year tenure with Milwaukee. The intent was to protect Giannis from emotional pain, not to stop the transaction. Giannis ultimately decided not to let the cautionary tale stop his move. The Trade Almost Fell Apart Unintentionally, Lillard’s “advice” could have denied the Heat the acquisition of Giannis. Once again, it seems both Giannis and Miami are in a superior position for now, yet assigning blame to Lillard for this specific brand of “wisdom” is difficult. The Heat nearly missed out on Giannis due to Lillard’s counsel. In theory, Lillard was simply trying to protect Giannis. After all, his own “move” away from his hometown Portland Trail Blazers did not work out. It resulted in a catastrophic Achilles injury, followed by his release and stretch by the organization. As a result, Lillard cautioned Giannis that decisions feeling correct in the moment could eventually backfire. item.description: Photo by Alex Goodlett/Getty Images Victor Wembanyama revealed that, like the greats, including LeBron James, he was not going to think about the ethics of scoring 50 points in an NBA game. The 22-year-old went off for 50 points and 18 rebounds on an efficient 69% shooting from the field, while also contributing with 4 steals and 5 blocks. In his walkoff interview, the French centre said: “Unlike many of my peers, I’m not very good at stat padding.” It was believed that Wembanyama’s comments were a dig at Luka Doncic, who is the only other player to score 50+ points twice this season. However, in his press conference, he explained his statement by revealing what the greats of the game thought about this. “The greats they don’t think about that, I don’t think Lebron, Shai, Jokic, Luka, I don’t think they think about that. I have them as examples, so I am not trying to think about it either,” said Wemby. He also went on to explain what ethical basketball meant to him, as he believed it was not a defined word. Victor Wembanyama agrees he wanted to get to 50 points His 50-pointer against the New Orleans Pelicans was the third for him in his career. He is now tied with David Robinson for the most 50-point games as a San Antonio Spurs player. While this is a terrific achievement, the two-time All-Star revealed what his thought process was while he was approaching the 50-point mark. “I did try to get the three up, when I had 47 points,” said Wemby. item.description: Check out the Brazil women's team's schedule for friendlies in Japan The Brazil Women's National Team will wrap up their 2026 schedule with two friendlies in Japan against the hosts. In April 2012, in the Kirin Challenge Cup, Japan won again, this time 4–1 at Kobe Wing Stadium in Kobe. The friendly in Hiroshima will therefore be the teams' third meeting on Japanese soil. Overall, the teams have faced each other 17 times, and the Amarelinha hold the edge: eight wins, two draws and seven defeats. Brazil have scored 23 goals and conceded 26. item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Nick Wright explores the possibility of a Los Angeles Lakers vs. Philadelphia 76ers matchup in the NBA Finals. LeBron James’ decision to part ways with the Los Angeles Lakers in the off-season and join the Philadelphia 76ers has worked out well for both sides. Nick Wright gives ‘non-zero’ verdict on a potential LA Lakers vs. Philadelphia 76ers Theoretically, the two sides can only meet in the playoffs during the NBA Finals. But do the two teams’ rosters have enough firepower to make it a reality? Well, according to sports analyst Nick Wright, the possibility is increasing with each passing game during the 2026-27 season. “There’s a non-zero chance we get a Lakers-Sixers NBA Finals. LeBron against the team that he just left. Unbelievable theater. “Philadelphia is clearly the favourites in the Eastern Conference. item.title: Current silence Rowdy Audi, Spirit fall short in final again: ‘It hurts way worse than the others’
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. — How much more can the Washington Spirit’s hearts break? Three championship appearances in the last three years. Three times those games ended with the Spirit left on the shadowy side of a shiny trophy. Every head of the steadfast Spirit supporters was downcast as they bobbed down the staircases exiting Audi Field after their 2-1 defeat to the Kansas City Current . Empty-handed once again. It wasn’t supposed to happen this way. After the Orlando Pride in 2024 and Gotham FC in 2025, the Spirit were meant to triumph on their third attempt at a championship. It was supposed to happen at Rowdy Audi, before many of the 19,365 people who flocked to the nation’s capital to be reminded that fairytale endings still existed in football. This journey was not meant to end with Trinity Rodman crumpled on the pitch with her head in her hands. The league created the now-defunct High Impact Player rule to keep Rodman, an MVP finalist this year, in the U.S. Instead, she suffered another painful loss. “Obviously, this one hurts way worse than any of the other ones,” Rodman said in the mixed zone after the game. “I don’t even think you have words in this moment. It’s too fresh.” The match was still fresh when Kansas City landed what may be remembered as the knockout punch. In the fifth minute, 24-year-old Current right-back Laney Rouse challenged Rodman near the touchline. Rouse, formerly of the University of Virginia, lunged with the whole side of her body and caught Rodman in the shoulder. “As a team, you always want to put the first tackle out,” Rodman said. “You’re taught to make the first hit. Credit to that, because I wish I was the one that put (Rouse) on the ground, but at the end of the day, I think they did a really good job of setting the tone and controlling a lot of the first half for sure.” Referee Joshua Encarnación did not issue any further caution apart from Rouse’s foul. Just like that, a precedent was set, and in the process Rouse accomplished something very few players can do at Rowdy Audi: she silenced it. The crowd had been booming since the warm-up. Current center-back Kayla Sharples said the pause in the game during Rodman’s treatment offered them a moment to regroup. “It did kind of get quiet after the initial fall, so we were actually able to communicate a little bit better, locking eyes with each other, trying to stay engaged and focused,” Sharples said. “Those were key moments.” Asked how her shoulder was feeling after the game, Rodman offered a dry smile. “Phenomonal.” When the crowd resumed, they jeered every teal-colored touch of the ball and unsavory challenge. They made it known every time a Spirit player was called for a foul they felt was unjust. By the 35th minute, 14 fouls had been called, split fairly evenly between the two. item.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Joe Joyce makes his pick after years of deliberation
item.description: On December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua is set to finally take place. The entire card will stream live and exclusively around the world on Netflix. It’s often felt like this fight would never happen, but everything is set for these two titans of British boxing to meet for the WBA “super” heavyweight title. As we edge closer to fight night, fellow British heavyweight Joe Joyce has spoken to The Ring , revealing his pick for Fury-Joshua. Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Joe Joyce makes his pick for December 11 Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) has been brilliant at times during his career. The game plan against Wladimir Klitschko was perfect, and later on, the tactics in the trilogy with Deontay Wilder were perfectly executed by “The Gypsy King.” He later tackled Oleksandr Usyk, losing twice to the Ukrainian. After losing the rematch to Oleksandr Usyk , Fury retired once again before returning to the ring earlier this year, beating Arslanbek Makhmudov and Mariusz Wach. Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) has been beloved by much of the British public since winning the gold medal at the 2012 Olympics. During his professional career, his best wins have come against Wladimir Klitschko, Alexander Povetkin, and Joseph Parker. In his most recent bout, AJ was floored twice in the opening round against Kristian Prenga, before stopping him in the second round. I firmly believe he has the power to do this; however, Fury seemingly still has the ability to box and move. Is Fury on the decline? Yes, his performance against Wach showed that. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
